slots.label: Heading 2
slots.default: Attacks that carry no malware at all

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Someone gets hold of a working username and password, often from a convincing phishing page, and simply logs in. Nothing has to be installed, so nothing gets flagged. From there the attacker uses tools that are already on the machine, which is why this approach is known as living off the land. To antivirus it all looks like normal admin work.

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: MDR looks at behaviour instead of file signatures. It is less interested in what a file is called and more interested in what is happening: an account signing in from two countries an hour apart, a process quietly turning off protection, files being encrypted in bulk, a workstation suddenly scanning the rest of the network. Those patterns are hard to disguise, because they are the attack itself rather than the tooling used to deliver it.
